(3) CONSEQUENCE - FALSE. OUR STATE says "There is no exclusive-control mode and therefore no way to express the documented 'disable MCP entirely' pattern - `deniedMcpServers` blocks only what it names." It examined only the denylist. The instrument for deny-all is the SIBLING list, and the same page documents it: managed-mcp.md:145 - "| `allowedMcpServers` | All servers allowed | No servers allowed | Only matching servers allowed |" for unset / empty array / populated. BUT the claim that there is "no way to express the documented 'disable MCP entirely' pattern" is false: it looked only at `deniedMcpServers`. The page's own table at managed-mcp.md:145 gives `allowedMcpServers: []` = "No servers allowed", and we implement exactly that - `parseManagedMcpEntryList` preserves the empty array (`managed-policy.ts:1307-1312`, `:1447`), `evaluateManagedMcpServer` (`managed-mcp-entries.ts:489-509`) then admits nothing, pinned by `managed-mcp-entries.test.ts:324,346`.
